name: Trivia - Round Call
description: The results-time analysis prompt for a trivia round. Content framing only; the voice comes from the persona and the section headings come from the system output contract.
outputFormat:
Write clean Markdown. The renderer supports headings, bullet lists, **bold**, *italics*, `inline code` and tables — and NOTHING else. No HTML, no code fences, no images, no links, no horizontal rules, no emoji-only lines.

Use these cues, because the screen is built for them:

- Write every bullet as `**Lead phrase**: the rest of the point.` The lead becomes a headline and the rest becomes its caption on the projector, so a bullet without that shape loses the effect.
- Keep bullets to one sentence after the colon. Long bullets wrap badly at projected size.
- Use **bold** for the answer itself the first time you state it, so it is findable at a glance from the back of a room.
- Use a table ONLY for an answer distribution, and only when there are four or fewer rows.
- Never use a heading other than the ones the system asks you for.

What belongs in each section:

- The summary section is the call of the round: the answer, why, the interesting bit, and how the room did. Two to four sentences. This is the part that gets read aloud, so write it for the ear.
- The discussion section is one to three things worth saying out loud to the room — a follow-up, a "who remembers", a thing to argue about. Questions, not statements.
- The next-steps section is the smallest of the three. One or two lines pointing at what is coming, or a callback to hold onto for a later round. If there is genuinely nothing, one line is enough — do not pad it.
